Accordingly, our respective Governments, through representatives assembled in the city of San Francisco, who have exhibited their full powers found to be in good and due form, have agreed to the present Charter of the United Nations and do hereby establish an international organization to be known as the United Nations.

related.excerpt: THE GENEV A CONVENTIONS OF 12 AUGUST 1949 THE GENEV A CONVENTIONS OF 12 AUGUST 1949 ICRC 0173/002 05.2010 10,000 Mission The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) is an impartial, neutral and independent organization whose exclusively humanitarian mission is to protect the lives and dignity of victims of armed conflict and other situations of violence and to provide them with assistance. The ICRC also endeavours to prevent suffering by promoting and strengthening humanitarian law and universal humanitarian principles. Established in 1863, the ICRC is at the origin of the Geneva Conventions and the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement. It directs and coordinates the international activities conducted by the Movement in armed conflicts and other situations of violence. United States Vice President JD Vance has been defending the memorandum of understanding to end the US-Israeli war with Iran, responding to criticism of the deal from members of the opposing Democratic Party and Republicans alike.

Several top Democrats – and a handful of Republicans – have said the initial agreement appears to favour Tehran, saying the war has yielded no meaningful concessions that could not have been achieved in previous rounds of diplomacy.
The vice president framed the war as a victory, regardless of whether the upcoming negotiations, which he said could begin as soon as the weekend, were successful.

The initial agreement also includes a commitment that Iran will dilute its stockpile of highly enriched uranium “on site”, but leaves questions related to the future of Iran’s nuclear programme unanswered, leaving the issue for 60 days of negotiations.

related.excerpt: FACTS & FIGURES OF THE INTERNATIONAL COMMITTEE OF THE RED CROSS IN LIBYA January - December – 2025 In 2025, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) in Libya has continued its humanitarian response to address the con- sequences of armed conflict and armed violence, and to support people affected by it, such as separated families, missing, detained or displaced people. The work has been defined by cooperation, capacity building, and material and infrastructure support in the fields of health, physical rehabilitation, hygiene, water access and forensics. The ICRC continued to provide productive grants and business training to con- flict-affected households to foster their financial autonomy. Key to our endeavor is ICRC’s role as guardian of International Humanitarian Law (IHL), the law of armed conflicts, in the terms entrusted to the ICRC by all States in the Geneva Conventions, which Libya ratified in 1956. The work has only been possible through the cooperation and support of the Libyan Red Crescent Society (LRCS) as well as the backing of the relevant authorities. related.excerpt: Libya in 2025: Standing alongside communities affected by conflict and violence In 2025, the humanitarian consequences of armed conflict continued to affect communities across Libya.
